clue.text: Explorer John heading off to the west on journey to see island

indicators.note: in an across clue westward is right to left, so the remaining letters are read backwards
the explorer's name loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer who sailed for England in 1497
to go is to journey

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip in the footsteps of an explorer to visit a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ABOT, which 'to the west' turns into TOBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Time passed quickly, held up by the incomplete ordinal

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: flew means passed quickly, as time does

indicators.note: the short word the loses its final letter, left unfinished

explanation.surface: A grumble that time flies while some unfinished ordinal number hangs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns FLEW into WELF, and 'incomplete' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal number gives position in a sequence, and number twelve in order is an example.

clue.text: See 19
Unsteady on a horse, encouragement given to it?

parts.note: giddy means dizzy and unsteady
up means riding, in the saddle, as in a jockey being up

explanation.surface: A rider wobbles in the saddle while calling out to urge the horse on.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders shout this phrase to urge a horse forward, so it is the encouragement addressed to the mount.

clue.text: See 19
Motor home finally, beginning to glide into square

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word home
into tells us the glide letter goes inside the square number

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of glide

explanation.surface: Someone motors home and, at the end, glides gently into a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives G, which 'into' places inside NINE to make NGINE after the E from 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is the machine that drives a vehicle, a synonym for the power unit.

clue.text: Tit well off with old tailless bird

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the word old loses its last letter, its tail

explanation.surface: A tit that is far from well sits beside an ageing bird missing its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts OLD to OL, and 'off' rearranges TITWELL with OL.
explanation.definitionFit: This small owl species is a common European bird, introduced to Britain in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Outstanding grammar ultimately, weirdo's imperfect tense

indicators.note: imperfect suggests the word is flawed and must be put right by rearranging its letters
ultimately points to the final letter of the word grammar

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which an odd pupil gets the imperfect tense badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar words 'imperfect tense' pose as one term; 'imperfect' rearranges R plus WEIRDO, and 'tense' is the definition. 'Outstanding' is a surface flourish praising the grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense as an adjective means anxious and on edge, a close synonym of nervous and fretful.

clue.text: John's getting stick reading "Reptile" at every bite?

definitions.text: John's getting stick reading "Reptile" at every bite?

parts.words: John's getting stick reading "Reptile" at every bite?
parts.note: an Elton John song pictured as a stick of seaside candy with a large reptile's name running through it, visible wherever you bite

explanation.surface: Elton John is handed a stick of seaside candy lettered with a reptile's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a hard British candy stick with a word printed all the way through, so every bite shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1972 Elton John hit fits the picture of a candy stick lettered with a reptile name.

clue.text: Still standing character, elusive beast

parts.note: yet means still, as in still to come
the letter I stands upright, a character standing

explanation.surface: A statue-still figure is spotted, perhaps the elusive mountain creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary creature that never lets itself be found.

clue.text: Stabbed from the right, a politician critical

indicators.note: read from the right means the word is written backwards

parts.note: gored means stabbed with a horn
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician is stabbed in the back by someone on the right, a critical moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the right' turns GORED into DEROG.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks are disparaging, the same sense as critical in a hostile way.

clue.text: Harsh cricket side confronting opener

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a key is what opens a lock

explanation.surface: A tough cricket team lines up against an opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-key music is out of tune and so grating, harsh on the ear.

clue.text: John's John didn't lie when condemned

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: condemned to ruin, the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone's John insists he told no lie when he was sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'condemned', with 'when' doubling as part of the fodder; CAN then precedes the rearranged DIDNTLIEWHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Elton John song, so it belongs to John, the theme setter of the puzzle.

clue.text: Force of life with droopy nuts getting treatment down below

parts.note: chi in Chinese thought is the vital life force

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the word is scrambled

explanation.surface: A healer combines life-force energy with a cure for sagging testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges DROOPY to ROPODY; 'down below' sounds intimate but means the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot care is medical attention to the lowest part of the body, hence treatment far down.

clue.text: John's John Glenn, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: an Elton John song, belonging to John
an astronaut, of whom Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth, is an example

explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut rides a rocket into space, and this is also an Elton John hit.

clue.text: See 19
The biter bit

definitions.meaning: a small bloodsucking arachnid that bites its host
a moment, as in just a bit or a second

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a parasite that bites and a brief instant of time.

clue.text: See 12
Those not out are unable to walk after bowled

indicators.note: after places the cricket letter before the rest

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
to lack legs is to be unable to walk

explanation.surface: Batsmen not out yet who cannot walk after being bowled, a cricket scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'not out' is still in; here those not out are workers who refuse to strike, scabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikebreakers keep working rather than coming out on strike, so they are not out.

clue.text: Token reply

definitions.meaning: a disc used in games or as a stand-in for money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gaming piece and a response or retort.

clue.text: John's "Hello Emerald City"?

parts.note: in the Wizard of Oz a famous path leads to the Emerald City, so greeting the city means leaving that path behind, an Elton John title

explanation.surface: Elton John greets the Emerald City of Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy follows a paved path to the Emerald City; arriving there means bidding the path farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1973 Elton John album and title song takes leave of the path to Oz.

clue.text: Fish starts to weaken, riding on the high seas

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of the next two words
high as in drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish weakening as it rides the waves out on the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish of the family Labridae.

clue.text: One passing on information concerned with French leader — sinner, might you say?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of French

parts.note: a sinner is one who errs, so might you call them an errer, a coined word

explanation.surface: An informant about a French leader who has sinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might you say' admits the invented ERRER, one who errs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refers a case passes details on to another person or body.

clue.text: Result, finished effort

parts.note: up means over, as in time is up
a shot is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: Reporting the outcome of a completed attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or final consequence is a synonym for result.

clue.text: John's most challenging word, it seems: not entirely kind, really hollow

definitions.text: John's most challenging word, it seems

indicators.note: the word for kind is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sort means kind or type

indicators.note: hollow means only the outer letters of really remain

explanation.surface: Someone's hardest word to say, seemingly, is neither quite kind nor truly heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Elton John song title Sorry Seems to Be the Hardest Word. 'not entirely' trims SORT to SOR; 'hollow' leaves RY of really.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John sang that this apology seems to be the hardest word to say.

clue.text: Small mice at sea, scattering — seeing this?

definitions.text: Small mice at sea, scattering — seeing this?

indicators.note: the mice scatter, so their letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Tiny mice on a ship flee in all directions because a predator is watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the mice scatter because they see the feline.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice would scatter on seeing this pale, blue-eyed breed of domestic feline.

clue.text: The assassin's assassin in a shade of red

definitions.meaning: Jack ... shot Lee Harvey Oswald, who killed President Kennedy
a deep red colour, like the gemstone

explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ruby killed Oswald, and the gemstone name is a deep crimson colour.

clue.text: John's in deal that's dodgy

indicators.note: a dodgy deal is crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Someone named John is in on a shady deal.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1973 Elton John single belongs to John, the theme of the puzzle.

clue.text: Knitting pattern barely grasped, a stretch when spinning

indicators.note: spinning turns the run of letters around, read backwards
a stretch of the phrase is taken, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A knitter barely grasps a stretch of wool as it spins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stretch' takes ELYGRA from barELY GRAsped; 'when spinning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This diamond pattern, from a Scottish clan tartan, is a classic design on socks and sweaters.
